record.paper_title: Seminar Notes on Open Questions in Iwasawa Theory - SNOQIT I: The Λ[G]-modules of Iwasawa theory II: Units and Kummer theory in Iwasawa extensions
record.original_question: For a CM Galois extension K containing the p-th roots of unity, is the minus-part T-torsion in the p-unit class-group module trivial; that is, does (A′)^−[T] = {1} hold? This is the classical Gross conjecture in the paper's formulation, expressing that the minus-part p-unit class module has no nontrivial T-torsion.

evidence.quote: This is a conjecture of Gross [3], which follows from the elementary lemma below and the decomposition A−[T] = (A′)−[T] ⊕ B−.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be a prime number and let $K$ be a CM number field containing the $p$-th roots of unity, with maximal totally real subfield $K^+$. Let $T$ be the (finite, non-empty) set of places of $K$ above $p$. Consider the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension $K_\infty/K$, write $K_n$ for its $n$-th layer, and let $\Gamma=\mathrm{Gal}(K_\infty/K)$.

For each $n$, let $A'_n$ denote the $p$-part of the $T$-class group of $K_n$, i.e. the $p$-Sylow subgroup of the ideal class group of the ring of $T$-integers $\mathcal{O}_{K_n,T}$ (equivalently, the quotient of the $p$-part of the full ideal class group by the classes generated by primes of $K_n$ above $p$). Let
$$A' \;=\; \varprojlim_n A'_n,$$
the projective limit taken with respect to the norm maps; this is a finitely generated module over the Iwasawa algebra $\Lambda = \mathbb{Z}_p[\![\Gamma]\!]$.

Complex conjugation $j\in\mathrm{Gal}(K/K^+)$ acts on $A'$, and since $p$ is odd one has the eigenspace decomposition $A' = (A')^+ \oplus (A')^-$, where $(A')^- = \{x\in A' : j(x) = -x\}$.

Let $T$ also denote, by abuse of notation, the closed subgroup of $A'$ generated topologically by classes coming from the decomposition groups of the primes above $p$ in $K_\infty/K$, and write $(A')^-[T]$ for the $T$-torsion submodule of the minus part $(A')^-$.

Prove or disprove: 
$$(A')^-[T] = \{1\}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The statement is known as the Gross (or Gross–Kuz'min) conjecture. It is equivalent to the non-vanishing of the $p$-adic regulator of $p$-units (Federer–Gross, 1981) and was proved by Greenberg (1973) for abelian extensions of $\mathbb{Q}$. In full generality for CM fields it is widely regarded as still open, though several partial and conditional results (e.g., Kolster, and conditional proofs assuming Leopoldt) and proposed proofs (e.g., the 2011 preprint "The Gross–Kuz'min conjecture for CM fields") exist; the conjecture in full generality has not been universally accepted as solved.

status_evidence.title: The Gross–Kuz'min conjecture for CM fields
status_evidence.snippet: The Gross-Kuz'min conjecture concerns the projective limit of the p-parts of ideal class groups in the Z_p-cyclotomic extension of a CM number field, claiming that (A')^-(T) = 0.
status_evidence.claim: The statement is the well-known Gross–Kuz'min conjecture, proved for abelian K/Q (Greenberg 1973), open in general for CM fields.

status_evidence.title: On a conjecture concerning minus parts in the style of Gross
status_evidence.snippet: Federer and Gross showed in 1981 that (A')^-(T) = 0 is equivalent to the non-vanishing of the p-adic regulator of the p-units of K.
status_evidence.claim: Equivalent to a non-vanishing p-adic regulator statement; partial results known.
